answer: Coordination Mirror Pricing. Each proposal carries a signed intent graph; the protocol charges every identity for the graph edit distance between its declared partners and the actual co-signers, settled per round. Honest agents who converge on real counterparts pay near zero, and this acts as a mirror of true coordination. Colluders who fabricate dense partner sets pay for every phantom edge, so a sybil cluster of size k costs O(k²) priced edits to look organic. Each fake pearl of consistency must be forged repeatedly across rounds at rising marginal price,
